archetypes.pitch: An aggressive BR tribe with a bloodthirsty, gothic vibe. Three Vampire lords and Edgar Markov build a fast curve while Blood tokens bridge into Madness synergies. For players who want a sleek, menacing aggro deck with plenty of synergy.
archetypes.rationale: Three lords plus Edgar's eminence over a deep aggressive Vampire curve; Blood tokens bridge into Madness.

archetypes.pitch: A BR aggro deck that turns discarding cards into free spells. Fiery Temper and friends cast at a discount off looting and Blood tokens, and hellbent payoffs love your empty hand. For players who enjoy reckless, fast, cost-cutting sequencing.
archetypes.rationale: Ten madness cards meet Blood tokens, looting, and escalate-discard costs; hellbent payoffs reward the empty hand.

archetypes.pitch: A UB tribe that just refuses to stay dead. Gravecrawler and undying bodies recur endlessly while Gisa and Geralf and Grimgrin turn them into a dominant board. For players who love grinding, resilient, self-recurring armies.
archetypes.rationale: Inherently recursive tribe (Gravecrawler, undying, self-return) converted into board dominance by lords and engines.

archetypes.pitch: A WU tempo deck full of flying flash threats. Mausoleum Wanderer and Spell Queller disrupt the opponent while evasive Spirits clock them out. For players who like slippery beatdown backed by counters and tricks.
archetypes.rationale: Flying flash bodies that disrupt while clocking; Tamiyo (cross-tag) draws off evasive attackers connecting.

archetypes.pitch: A RG midrange tribe that flips into huge threats when the game slows. Transforming werewolves like Huntmaster of the Fells swing games while payoffs count your growing pack. For players who like beefy creatures with a transforming payoff.
archetypes.rationale: Full curve of flip werewolves plus payoffs counting Wolves and Werewolves; Garruk's Wolf tokens (cross-tag) feed those counts.

archetypes.pitch: A wide, aggressive GW tribe with the deepest creature pool in the cube. Cheap Humans, token engines, and lords like Odric flood the board and pile on keywords. For players who love classic go-wide aggro.
archetypes.rationale: Widest tribe: cheap bodies, two Human-token engines, Human-specific rewards (Cleaver lifelink, Mayor's anthem), Odric keyword soup.

archetypes.pitch: The deepest sacrifice deck in the cube, turning dying creatures into drain and value. The Meathook Massacre and Blood Artist punish every death while free outlets fuel the engine. For players who love grindy, board-eating value decks.
archetypes.rationale: Deepest cluster (59 tagged): death payoffs, free outlets, recursive fodder; Zealous Conscripts (cross-tag) turns any outlet into removal.

archetypes.pitch: A UR tempo-control deck that doubles every spell with flashback. Thing in the Ice and Docent of Perfection flip into threats as you chain instants and sorceries. For players who love spell-heavy decks and explosive payoff turns.
archetypes.rationale: Flashback doubles every spell for the count-spells payoffs; Galvanic Iteration copying Temporal Mastery (cross-tag) is the haymaker.

archetypes.pitch: A white-based go-wide deck that pairs a huge board with anthems. Cathars' Crusade and Intangible Virtue make your tokens lethal, and Second Harvest doubles the swarm. For players who love flooding the board and overrunning the table.
archetypes.rationale: 44 token cards feed anthem payoffs; Unnatural Growth and Decimator (cross-tag) are go-wide finishers; Tamiyo's Journal Clues are tokens for Second Harvest.

archetypes.pitch: A BG midrange-combo deck that turns its graveyard into a resource. Splinterfright and The Gitrog Monster grow off creatures in the yard, and Hermit Druid plus Laboratory Maniac is a real combo kill. For players who like filling the bin and cashing it in.
archetypes.rationale: Payoffs scale with creature cards in yard while a dozen enablers stock it; Hermit Druid plus Laboratory Maniac is a real win line.

archetypes.pitch: A midrange-combo deck that cheats out Eldrazi by eating your own creatures. Emerge threats devour undying fodder to hit the board ahead of schedule. For players who like a resourceful, sacrifice-fueled ramp plan.
archetypes.rationale: Six cast-trigger Eldrazi eat undying/self-returning fodder; Heartless Summoning (cross-tag) discounts the fatties harmlessly.

archetypes.pitch: A WU value deck that resets enter-the-battlefield effects. Restoration Angel and Deadeye Navigator re-trigger a board full of ETB creatures for endless advantage. For players who enjoy value engines and answering everything.
archetypes.rationale: Four repeatable blink engines reset a cube full of ETB triggers; Helvault (fringe cross-tag) banks ETB creatures for a mass re-entry.

archetypes.pitch: A WB midrange deck that turns steady life gain into payoffs. Voice of the Blessed and Chalice of Life reward the drain and incidental gain from aristocrats effects. For players who like a resilient, grinding game plan.
archetypes.rationale: Two true gain-life payoffs over repeatable incidental gain; black drain effects double-dip.

archetypes.pitch: A white-based deck that suits up one creature and swings for the win. Recursive auras dodge card disadvantage while Sigarda gives an unkillable target to load up. For players who like all-in single-threat beatdown.
archetypes.rationale: Recursive/disturb auras dodge the 2-for-1; Sigarda's hexproof (cross-tag) is the ideal suit-up target.

archetypes.pitch: A BG midrange deck that turns land drops and dead lands into cards. The Gitrog Monster and Wrenn and Seven grind value while Cultivator Colossus is the big payoff. For players who love a slow, inevitable value grind.
archetypes.rationale: Gitrog and Wrenn convert land drops and dead lands into cards; Cultivator Colossus is the mass payoff.

archetypes.pitch: A GW aggro-midrange deck that grows its team through training and coven. Torens makes tokens that pump each other and Hopeful Initiate spends counters as removal. For players who like a snowballing, synergistic board.
archetypes.rationale: Torens' training tokens grow each other; Hopeful Initiate spends counters as removal; Mimic seeds any tribe.

archetypes.pitch: A black combo-midrange deck that drops giants ahead of schedule. Edgar's Awakening reanimates anything and Through the Breach cheats Griselbrand from hand. For players who want explosive, game-warping early plays.
archetypes.rationale: Edgar's Awakening reanimates anything; Breach cheats Griselbrand from hand; Mass Hysteria (cross-tag) gives the fatty haste. Breach does not cast, so cast-trigger Eldrazi get nothing.

archetypes.pitch: A build-around that fuses two cards into a single monster. All three meld pairs are here, and since each half plays fine alone, going for the meld is pure upside. For players who enjoy a rewarding two-card payoff.
archetypes.rationale: All three meld pairs and their melded faces are in the cube; each half is independently playable, so meld is pure upside.

archetypes.pitch: A quirky black combo that wins off an exact life total. Tree of Perdition sets the opponent to 13 and Triskaidekaphobia finishes them on your upkeep. A spicy build-around for players who love an unusual alternate win.
archetypes.rationale: Tree sets an opponent to exactly 13; Triskaidekaphobia's upkeep trigger then wins the game outright.

decks.strategy: Aristocrats/Sacrifice Midrange with Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia combo finisher
decks.identity: Mono-Black Aristocrats/Sacrifice Midrange with a Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia alternate win condition
decks.pitch: A mono-Black Aristocrats/Sacrifice Midrange deck. The primary plan is cheap fodder creatures feeding sacrifice outlets (Indulgent Aristocrat, Falkenrath Torturer, Ecstatic Awakener, Skirsdag High Priest) into a wall of death-trigger payoffs (Blood Artist, Morbid Opportunist, The Meathook Massacre, Restless Bloodseeker), grinding out games on card advantage and incremental drain. Riding on top of that engine is a two-card alternate win condition: Tree of Perdition (a 0/13 Defender) taps to set an opponent's life total to exactly 13, and Triskaidekaphobia kills any player sitting at exactly 13 life on its controller's upkeep. Westvale Abbey gives the deck a completely independent third finisher, transforming a wide board of expendable fodder into an indestructible flying lifelink threat.

decks.identity: Mono-black combo-control built around Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia, backed by a dense removal/death-trigger attrition shell.
decks.pitch: Slot allocation. Macro-Archetype: Control. Projected avg MV 2.71. Lands: 16 (40% of N=40) — mono-color needs no fixing buffer, and the low curve (nothing above 5, half the deck at CMC<=2) lets a control shell run lean; the mana audit confirms 16/16 recommended, PASS. Of the 24 nonland slots: Interaction 11 cards (45.8%) — sweepers/removal/disruption (Meathook Massacre, Collective Brutality, Invasion of Innistrad, Tragic Slip x2, Infernal Grasp x2, Murderous Compulsion, Eaten Alive, Sever the Bloodline, Morkrut Banshee), slightly above the 35-45% reference band because this deck has almost no independent "threats" — removal density has to cover for that. Payoffs 3 cards (12.5%) — Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia x2, the actual win condition. Engine/Infrastructure 10 cards (41.7%) — Cryptolith Fragment x2, Sorin, Blood Artist x2, Morbid Opportunist x2, and the recursive/undying blocker suite (Sanitarium Skeleton, Butcher Ghoul, Epitaph Golem); this runs above the 10-20% reference band because in this build the blockers *are* the engine — every one of them dies profitably into Blood Artist/Morbid Opportunist/morbid triggers rather than just soaking damage.

decks.identity: Black-Green sacrifice value deck: recursive/undying fodder into free sac outlets, closing with Skirsdag High Priest, Garruk Relentless, and Westvale Abbey.
decks.pitch: Engine math. Dedicated fodder bodies are thin (5: Gravecrawler, Sanitarium Skeleton, 2x Young Wolf, Butcher Ghoul) but the deck supplements them with self-replacing token generation — Ghoulish Procession and Ulvenwald Mysteries both trigger only on *nontoken* creature deaths, so the fodder base (all nontoken) feeds them cleanly, but the tokens they produce don't feed back into either engine. Six outlets (Village Rites x2, Ecstatic Awakener, Falkenrath Torturer, Eaten Alive, Demonmail Hauberk's equip cost, Garruk's -1) are available to convert that fodder into value.

decks.identity: Black-Green midrange grind built around The Gitrog Monster and Wrenn and Seven — self-mill and recur lands to fuel repeated card draw, landfall value, and graveyard-scaling threats.
decks.pitch: The core loop. Every self-mill effect (Eccentric Farmer, Grapple with the Past, Moldgraf Millipede's ETB, Splinterfright's upkeep trigger) puts lands into the graveyard, which The Gitrog Monster turns into a card each time. Groundskeeper, Grapple, Traverse the Ulvenwald, and Wrenn and Seven's +1/0 modes all buy those lands back, refueling extra land drops (Gitrog) and repeated landfall triggers (Tireless Tracker). This is a closed loop, not a one-shot value creature — it keeps compounding as long as the deck has lands left to cycle.

decks.strategy: Pure Combo - Hermit Druid + Laboratory Maniac
decks.identity: BG combo splashing U, running zero basic lands so Hermit Druid mills its entire library into the graveyard, then recurring Laboratory Maniac with Crawl from the Cellar to win off any draw effect.
decks.pitch: Deck identity. This is a glass-cannon Pure Combo build: Hermit Druid ({G}, T: reveal until a basic land, put it to hand, everything else to the graveyard) is backed by zero basic lands in the 40, so its one activation mills the entire remaining library. Crawl from the Cellar (flashback {3}{B}, castable straight from the graveyard) then returns Laboratory Maniac from the graveyard to hand; casting it turns on "if you would draw with an empty library, you win instead." Any unconditional draw effect - Think Twice (also flashback-able from the graveyard) or Village Rites (sacrifice the now-tapped Hermit Druid) - closes the game. Everything else in the 40 exists to find, protect, or fund that four-piece sequence.

decks.strategy: Hermit Druid + Laboratory Maniac combo (BG core, U splash)
decks.identity: BG(u) self-mill combo/value deck: ramp and tutors assemble Hermit Druid + Laboratory Maniac while a basic-depletion package strips the manabase's few basics from the library so a later Druid activation empties it; Crawl from the Cellar recurs Laboratory Maniac and any of several draw effects wins.
decks.pitch: Honest timeline (this is the important part). This cube's BG(u) nonbasic land pool is thin - only 6 dual lands total across BG/GU/BU (2 per pair). A true zero-basic Hermit Druid build would cap out around 7-9 real lands, which was rejected as too fragile in favor of a healthier 15-land manabase. This list runs 7 basics (4 Forest/3 Swamp). Two rounds of self-grill quantified what that costs: with 7 basics in the library, a single early Hermit Druid activation only mills through roughly 5-8 cards on average (using the (N+1)/(K+1) expected-position formula for the first "success" in a shuffled deck), not the whole library. The basic-depletion package (Traverse the Ulvenwald, Evolving Wilds, Traveler's Amulet, Wild-Field Scarecrow) meaningfully improves this - each is a permanent, one-way removal of a basic from the library - but they're all singletons, so the odds of drawing all four by turn 8 are under 2%. The realistic plan is a multi-turn grind: Hermit Druid activating turn after turn (each activation removes at least the one basic it stops on) until the basics run out organically, landing a genuine full mill around turn 9-13, occasionally earlier (roughly 10-20% of games) if the depletion tools or lucky self-mill hits come together faster. This is a real, working combo-value deck - just not a same-turn instant kill. The tradeoff for a faster line is reverting toward a stricter zero-basic land base (~9 lands), accepting a thinner manabase.

decks.identity: Black-Green midrange where land recursion (Groundskeeper, Grapple with the Past, Eccentric Farmer) doubles as card advantage through The Gitrog Monster and Wrenn and Seven, with Tireless Tracker and Cultivator Colossus as top-end payoffs and a self-mill graveyard package (Splinterfright, Moldgraf Millipede, Spider Spawning) as a secondary win condition.
decks.pitch: The engine loop. Groundskeeper (x2) returns basic lands from graveyard to hand; Grapple with the Past (x2) mills 3 and can grab a land or creature back; Eccentric Farmer mills 3 on ETB and does the same. That's 5 dedicated pieces recycling lands, each replay triggering The Gitrog Monster's "land card into graveyard, draw" and Tireless Tracker's landfall investigate. Evolving Wilds doubles as a Gitrog trigger (sacrificing it puts a land in the graveyard) and a landfall trigger (fetching a basic onto the battlefield) in the same activation.

decks.identity: Black-Green self-mill midrange: mill enablers stock the graveyard, then Splinterfright/Ghoultree/Emrakul cash it in as size and cost discounts, with The Gitrog Monster and Grizzly Ghoul converting the fallout into cards and bodies.
decks.pitch: Delirium math. The deck naturally sees 5 card types in the graveyard (Creature, Land, Instant, Sorcery, Enchantment via The Meathook Massacre) — comfortably clearing delirium's 4-type threshold by turn 4-5 in most games. That flips Traverse the Ulvenwald from a 1-mana basic-land tutor into a 1-mana creature-or-land tutor, and drives Emrakul, the Promised End's real-world cast cost down from a nominal {13} to roughly {8} once a few permanent types are in the yard.

decks.identity: Black-Green self-mill into token swarm with U splash for Vilespawn Spider activation
decks.pitch: Self-mill density is 11 enablers (44% of non-lands): Hermit Druid, Splinterfright x2, Moldgraf Millipede x2, Eccentric Farmer x2, Grapple with the Past x2, Vilespawn Spider, and Noose Constrictor as a discard outlet. With this many enablers, the graveyard reliably stocks 6-10 creatures by turn 5, making Spider Spawning produce a lethal token army from a single cast -- and flashback provides a second wave.

decks.identity: Black-Red sacrifice deck: cheap fodder into free outlets into death-trigger payoffs, with a light White splash for Archangel Avacyn.
decks.pitch: The engine loop. Ten cards in this list are outlets or fodder-producers that trigger on demand: Village Rites, Falkenrath Torturer (x2), Indulgent Aristocrat (x2), Bloodtithe Harvester (x2, both as an ETB Blood-token maker and a self-sacrificing removal spell), plus Zealous Conscripts feeding a stolen creature into any of the above. That's enough density that Morbid (Tragic Slip, Skirsdag High Priest) and the death-payoffs (Blood Artist x2, Morbid Opportunist x2, The Meathook Massacre) are live most turns from turn 2 onward.

decks.identity: BR graveyard-combo hybrid using discard outlets to stock the graveyard, then cheating Griselbrand into play via Through the Breach or reanimating with Edgar's Awakening. Recursive Zombie fodder provides early board, emerge fuel, and card-engine triggers.
decks.pitch: This deck operates on two axes: sorcery-speed hard reanimation via Edgar's Awakening and instant-speed haste cheating via Through the Breach. With nine distinct discard effects across fourteen cards, the probability of seeing both a big target and an outlet in the first few turns is high in a 40-card format.

decks.strategy: BR discard/reanimator midrange - cheat/reanimate Griselbrand via Through the Breach and Edgar's Awakening
decks.identity: Black-primary/Red-secondary discard shell that weaponizes Griselbrand via ~9 discard outlets and two redundant cheat/reanimate lines
decks.pitch: The two lines to Griselbrand aren't equivalent - know which one you're playing. Through the Breach puts Griselbrand into play from hand for {4}{R}, but its own text sacrifices the creature at the beginning of the next end step - it's a one-turn burst, not a stable threat. You get one attack and however many "Pay 7 life: Draw seven cards" activations your life total allows, then it's gone. Edgar's Awakening (x2) is the permanent line: it returns a creature from the graveyard to the battlefield outright, and stays there. If you've discarded Griselbrand, Edgar's Awakening is the reliable path; Through the Breach is best used when Griselbrand is stuck in hand (or was returned there via Edgar's Awakening's own discard-triggered ability, which recurs a creature to hand, not itself, when Edgar's Awakening is discarded).

decks.identity: BR low-curve tempo deck: discard-into-madness value package (Faithless Looting, Lightning Axe, Collective Brutality, Blood tokens) backed by dual-purpose removal/burn and a hellbent-payoff top end (Bloodhall Priest, Bedlam Reveler).
decks.pitch: A low-curve BR shell built around discarding madness cards into cheap value: Faithless Looting, Lightning Axe, Collective Brutality's escalate, and repeatable Blood tokens (Voldaren Epicure, Bloodtithe Harvester) all convert a card in hand into a discounted madness spell. The actual win condition is combat damage from an efficient 11-creature suite backed by dual-purpose removal/burn (several spells also hit the opponent's face), with Bloodhall Priest and Bedlam Reveler as top-end payoffs for emptying the hand.

decks.identity: Black-Red-Green reanimator: discard/mill Griselbrand into the graveyard and bring him back via Edgar's Awakening, or cheat him in with Through the Breach; Hermit Druid and green ramp/fixing support the plan with backup fatties (Ghoultree, Bramble Wurm).
decks.pitch: Macro-Archetype: Combo. Projected Avg CMC: 3.0.

decks.identity: Mono-Black combo-control built around Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia
decks.pitch: This deck executes a two-card deterministic win in 40-card limited: Tree of Perdition sets an opponent to exactly 13 life, and Triskaidekaphobia's upkeep trigger kills any player at exactly 13. The combo is mana-efficient (4B + 4B) and can be deployed as early as turn 5 with a clean curve.

decks.identity: GW Sigarda Voltron: suit up a resilient or evasive body with recursive auras and scaling equipment that dodge single removal spells via undying/disturb/graveyard-reattachment, then close fast. Odric, Lunarch Marshal shares granted keywords across the team.
decks.pitch: Macro-Archetype: Aggro. Projected Avg MV: 2.12.

decks.strategy: Mono-Black Aristocrats/Graveyard Value Midrange with Griselbrand/Edgar's Awakening reanimation top-end
decks.identity: Black sacrifice-value midrange that converts creature deaths into card draw, life drain, and bodies, topped off by a hardcast/reanimated Griselbrand.
decks.pitch: A black sacrifice-value midrange deck that turns every creature death — combat trades, sac-outlet activations, Meathook Massacre wipes — into card draw, life drain, and bodies. Griselbrand and Edgar's Awakening form the deck's "Reanimator" top-end: Griselbrand is a hardcast bomb that refuels the hand, and Edgar's Awakening is a direct reanimation spell that can bring back Griselbrand (or any dead value creature) from the graveyard. The archetype context's original Reanimator/Breach shell didn't survive contact with the cube's actual card pool (see below) and the deck pivoted to lean on this cube's genuinely deep black Aristocrats/Graveyard support instead.

decks.strategy: Go-Wide Wolf Tokens Aggro (flip werewolves + Wolf token payoffs)
decks.identity: Red-Green werewolf-flip aggro with 100% Wolf/Werewolf creature density, closing games via Wolf-count payoffs and Second Harvest token doubling
decks.pitch: Every werewolf keystone in this cube (Huntmaster of the Fells, Arlinn Kord, Mayor of Avabruck, Kruin Outlaw) stacks into the same plan: flip early, generate 2/2 Wolf tokens, and let Runebound Wolf / Moonlight Hunt / Howlpack Resurgence scale off however many Wolves and Werewolves are on the table. All 15 mainboard creatures are Wolf- or Werewolf-typed, so every payoff is live off the full curve, not a subset. Second Harvest is the one splurge slot — it doubles the token board Mayor/Huntmaster/Pack Guardian/Arlinn have already built, turning a wide board into a lethal one in a single instant.

decks.identity: RG Werewolves & Wolves: transform flip-werewolves by holding spell-free turns, then win with Wolf/Werewolf-count payoffs and anthems.
decks.pitch: Environment & pipeline. This cube is a balanced 5-color draft environment (each color ~12-13% of cards, no domain/kicker density) with strong graveyard/aristocrats/flashback support. UB has solid fixing (2x common Contaminated Aquifer). Three materially different Zombie sub-archetypes were viable in this pool — Gisa and Geralf value engine, Rooftop Storm explosive curve-out, and Grimgrin aristocrats (already built in this cube as ub-zombies-aristocrats) — and the Gisa and Geralf path was selected.

decks.identity: Suit up a cheap evasive/hasty creature with removal-resistant equipment and recursive auras, protect it, and close with a keyword-soup burst.
decks.pitch: Slot allocation. Macro-Archetype: Aggro. Projected Avg MV: ~2.3. Lands: 15 (37.5% of N=40) — one land above the 30-35% aggro band, deliberately: the deck has real non-hardcast mana sinks (Gryff's Boon buyback at {3}{W}, Angelfire Ignition flashback at {2}{R}{W}, equip costs up to {3}) plus a real 4-5 CMC tail (Markov Waltzer, Restoration Angel, Archangel Avacyn). Modifiers: no cantrips, no mana dorks, no MDFCs in this pool — 0 adjustment. Threats/Payoffs (creatures 13 + equipment/auras 8 + Angelfire Ignition 1 = 22 of 25 nonland, 88%) — voltron decks fold nearly everything into the payoff category since equipment/auras *are* the win condition, not a separate engine. Interaction (Valorous Stance x2 + Lightning Axe = 3 of 25, 12%) sits in the 10-15% aggro band.

decks.identity: RW tempo-burn-aggro deck built around Zealous Conscripts as the closing payoff: efficient cheap beaters and a dense removal/burn suite (Lightning Axe, Fiery Temper, Abrade, Vexing Devil, Chandra Dressed to Kill) clear blockers and apply reach, then Zealous Conscripts steals the opponent's best remaining blocker and swings with haste for the win.
decks.pitch: RW tempo-burn-aggro built around Zealous Conscripts as the closing payoff: a curve of efficient 1-3 drop beaters (Thraben Inspector, Vexing Devil, Voldaren Epicure, Blood Petal Celebrant, Lightning Mauler) clears the way with a dense removal/burn suite (Lightning Axe, Fiery Temper, Abrade, Valorous Stance, Chandra, Dressed to Kill), and Zealous Conscripts closes games by stealing the opponent's best remaining blocker, untapping it, and swinging with haste alongside the rest of the board.

decks.identity: UB Zombie synergy engine (Rooftop Storm free-cast + Necroduality copy) inside a graveyard/aristocrats shell, closing with Grimgrin, Corpse-Born
decks.pitch: The Necroduality + Drunau Corpse Trawler interaction is the deck's single biggest blowout. Casting Drunau Corpse Trawler (a nontoken Zombie) with Necroduality in play triggers Necroduality on Drunau's own ETB, creating a token copy of Drunau - which itself has an ETB that makes a 2/2 Zombie token, and Necroduality's copy trigger fires again off that copied Drunau's ETB too. Net result from one 4-mana creature: the original Drunau, a token copy of Drunau, and two 2/2 Zombie tokens - four bodies from a single card, all immediately available as Grimgrin sac fuel or Ghoulish Procession triggers. Haunted Dead behaves the same way (copy makes a second Spirit token).

decks.identity: Black-heavy UB Zombies aristocrats deck: Grimgrin, Corpse-Born is a repeatable sacrifice-outlet payoff fueled by recursive Zombie fodder and death-trigger engines (Blood Artist, Archghoul of Thraben, Ghoulish Procession, The Meathook Massacre).
decks.pitch: Grimgrin, Corpse-Born is the payoff: it enters tapped and only untaps when you sacrifice a creature, growing a counter and destroying a blocker every attack. Gravecrawler, Village Rites, and a full suite of death-triggered engines (Ghoulish Procession, Archghoul of Thraben, Blood Artist, The Meathook Massacre) turn every death in the deck into card advantage, life swings, and fresh Zombie bodies. Bladestitched Skaab anthems the go-wide fodder base, and six efficient black removal spells keep the board clear while the engine spins up.

decks.strategy: Gisa and Geralf value engine (Zombie graveyard-recursion midrange)
decks.identity: UB Zombie tribal built around Gisa and Geralf (free-cast a Zombie from graveyard each turn) and Necroduality (token-copy every nontoken Zombie ETB), fueled by self-mill and recursive Zombie ETB creatures.
decks.pitch: Environment & pipeline. This cube is a balanced 5-color draft environment (each color ~12-13% of cards, no domain/kicker density) with strong graveyard/aristocrats/flashback support. UB has solid fixing (2x common Contaminated Aquifer). Three materially different Zombie sub-archetypes were viable in this pool — Gisa and Geralf value engine, Rooftop Storm explosive curve-out, and Grimgrin aristocrats (already built in this cube as ub-zombies-aristocrats) — and the Gisa and Geralf path was selected.

decks.identity: Black-leaning UGB sacrifice deck: renewable/recursive fodder feeds six Emerge Eldrazi payoffs while aristocrats death triggers (Blood Artist, Meathook Massacre, Morbid Opportunist, Demonic Taskmaster) convert the constant sacrificing into extra value.
decks.pitch: The color field vs. color identity gap. The six Emerge Eldrazi print with a fully generic mana cost ({7}, {8}, {8}, {8}, {8}, {10}) -- their `colors` field is empty ("C" in the tables above) because none of their symbols live in the printed cost. Their actual color comes entirely from the Emerge alternative cost text: Elder Deep-Fiend's Emerge is `{5}{U}{U}`, Distended Mindbender's is `{5}{B}{B}`, Decimator of the Provinces's is `{6}{G}{G}{G}`. This is why the deck is genuinely 3-color despite half its creature base showing "colorless" in a strict mana-cost table -- and why the mana base carries meaningfully more U/G support (6 sources each) than the visible spell count alone would justify.

decks.strategy: UGB Emerge Eldrazi - Go-Wide Token Swarm
decks.identity: Six colorless Emerge Eldrazi finishers fueled by undying/self-returning fodder and token generators, with Blood Artist and Morbid Opportunist monetizing the resulting sacrifice loop.
decks.pitch: Six colorless Emerge Eldrazi are the finishers: sacrifice a creature, pay a reduced generic cost, get a cast-trigger. Cheap undying/self-returning fodder (Young Wolf, Butcher Ghoul, Biolume Egg) and token generators (Ghoulish Procession, Skirsdag High Priest, Vilespawn Spider, Drunau Corpse Trawler) keep feeding the sacrifice engine, while Blood Artist and Morbid Opportunist turn every one of those deaths into life drain and card advantage. Cryptolith Rite converts the resulting board into mana to help close the gap on Elder Deep-Fiend's UU, Distended Mindbender's BB, and Decimator's GGG.

decks.strategy: Emerge Eldrazi payoffs fed by undying/recursive sac fodder and a self-mill/graveyard-ramp support shell
decks.identity: Sacrifice cheap undying and recursive creatures to cast six colorless Emerge Eldrazi at a steep discount, using self-mill and Cryptolith Rite to fuel and fix a grindy three-color ramp shell.
decks.pitch: The Emerge math. Emerge costs are reduced by the sacrificed creature's mana value: sac a Young Wolf (MV1) into Elder Deep-Fiend (Emerge {5}{U}{U}) and you're casting an 8-mana flash mass-tap effect for {4}{U}{U} — 6 total mana, achievable turn 5-6 with any ramp online. Sac a Butcher Ghoul (MV2) instead and it drops to {3}{U}{U} (5 mana). Because Young Wolf and Butcher Ghoul are both undying, and Gravecrawler recurs from the yard as long as a Zombie (Butcher Ghoul qualifies) is in play, the fodder base regenerates instead of running out — this is what lets the deck realistically cast 2-3 Eldrazi in a long game instead of just one.

decks.strategy: Hermit Druid -> Laboratory Maniac combo backed by a self-mill/delirium creature beatdown plan
decks.identity: Green-Blue self-mill combo-midrange: Hermit Druid + Laboratory Maniac as an alternate win condition, with Splinterfright/Moldgraf Millipede/Ghoultree providing an independent fair beatdown clock off the same graveyard-filling core.
decks.pitch: This deck has two independently sufficient paths to victory built on the same 25-card core. Hermit Druid ({G}, {T}: reveal until a basic land, mill the rest) drains the library every activation; Laboratory Maniac (x2) converts the next forced draw into an instant win once the library is thin or empty. When the combo pieces aren't assembled yet, the exact same self-mill actions (Grapple with the Past, Eccentric Farmer, Deranged Assistant, Grizzled Angler, Splinterfright's passive upkeep mill) that drain the library also grow Splinterfright and Moldgraf Millipede and discount Ghoultree into a cheap 9/9 trampler — the fair beatdown plan and the combo plan share a mana base, a curve, and almost every card in the deck.

decks.strategy: UR flashback/graveyard-value midrange with an extra-turn combo finisher (Galvanic Iteration copying Miracled Temporal Mastery)
decks.identity: UR spells-matter deck: graveyard/flashback value engine (Thermo-Alchemist, Docent of Perfection, Burning Vengeance, Bedlam Reveler, Faithless Looting/Think Twice) with three independent win angles — incremental burn, token/anthem pressure, and a graveyard-scaling finisher — plus a bonus 2-extra-turn combo via Galvanic Iteration + Temporal Mastery.
decks.pitch: This is a UR spells-matter deck built on a graveyard/flashback value engine with a bonus extra-turn combo finisher. The headline play — Galvanic Iteration copying a Miracled Temporal Mastery — nets TWO extra turns from a single draw step (both the original and the copy resolve independently), but the deck doesn't depend on assembling that 2-card combo to win. Thermo-Alchemist, Docent of Perfection, and Burning Vengeance turn every instant/sorcery cast (including flashback recasts) into incremental damage or board presence, while Seize the Storm and Rise from the Tides convert a stocked graveyard into a late finisher. Faithless Looting and Think Twice keep the engine fed.

decks.identity: UR midrange casting cheap instants/sorceries (many with Flashback) to power Thing in the Ice, Docent of Perfection, Thermo-Alchemist/Delver, and Bedlam Reveler, with a Galvanic Iteration + Temporal Mastery extra-turn line as upside.
decks.pitch: Docent's transform is self-sufficient. "Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, create a 1/1 blue Human Wizard creature token. Then if you control three or more Wizards, transform this creature." The tokens it makes ARE Wizards, so Docent flips itself off 3 spell casts with no external Wizard support needed — this isn't a soft dependency, it's a closed loop.

decks.strategy: Izzet (UR) tempo-control anchored on Thing in the Ice, feat. Flashback/Spellslinger sub-themes
decks.identity: UR tempo-control: freeze the board behind Thing in the Ice and cheap interaction, win with Chandra/Jace/Docent of Perfection top-end and Burning Vengeance/Thermo-Alchemist incidental damage.
decks.pitch: Thing in the Ice is the pipeline anchor: a 2-mana Defender that counts down four ice counters off your own instant/sorcery casts, then flips into a 7/8 that bounces the whole board. Everything else either feeds that clock (cheap interaction, two flashback cantrips), protects it while it's a wall, or turns "cast a spell" into incremental damage (Thermo-Alchemist, Burning Vengeance, Docent of Perfection). Chandra and Jace are the control top-end once the board is frozen; Galvanic Iteration is the value multiplier tying the Spellslinger and Flashback halves of the plan together.

decks.identity: UR tempo-value deck built around Thing in the Ice's mass-bounce reset and Bedlam Reveler/Burning Vengeance's flashback grind, with Docent of Perfection and Rise from the Tides/Seize the Storm as graveyard-scaling token payoffs and Galvanic Iteration + Temporal Mastery as a bonus extra-turn combo finish.
decks.pitch: A tempo-value hybrid built around casting cheap instants and sorceries twice. Thing in the Ice counts down off spellcasting into a one-sided board wipe that spares your own Horror creatures; Docent of Perfection turns every spell into a Wizard token and eventually an anthem; Faithless Looting and flashback recursion stock the graveyard to fuel Bedlam Reveler's discount, Burning Vengeance's recurring damage, and Rise from the Tides / Seize the Storm's graveyard-scaling finishers. Galvanic Iteration copying a Miracled Temporal Mastery is the top-end haymaker -- two extra turns in one turn -- but the deck wins without it just as often through grind and reach.

decks.identity: UR Spellslinger Tempo — chain cheap cantrips and flashback spells to flip Thing in the Ice, untap Thermo-Alchemist, power out Bedlam Reveler, and trigger Burning Vengeance for repeated burn.
White-Blue Voltron: recursive/self-replacing auras and equipment suit up cheap evasive creatures, protected by flash bodies, counterspells, blink, and bounce.
decks.pitch: Redundancy against the 2-for-1. The archetype's core risk is a removal spell eating a creature and its attached payoff in one shot. This build stacks four independent dodges: (1) Gryff's Boon recurs itself from the graveyard for {3}{W}; (2) Twinblade Geist and Lantern Bearer both disturb into a second, aura-form threat; (3) Harvest Hand converts itself into a permanent Equipment on death; (4) equipment in general (Neglected Heirloom, Stitcher's Graft) survives the creature's death outright and just needs a cheap re-equip. Between these, 7 of the 9 payoff slots have some form of resilience built in — the deck rarely loses a full turn's investment to a single removal spell.

decks.identity: Mono-White Humans-flavored go-wide tokens aggro; anthems and Cathars' Crusade/Odric close games via board width.
decks.pitch: Curve & density. CMC distribution: 3 @ 1, 7 @ 2, 8 @ 3, 5 @ 4, 1 @ 5 (avg 2.75). Only Gather the Townsfolk makes tokens immediately off the cast; Dauntless Cathar and Mausoleum Guard convert deaths into bodies, so the deck's width comes from bodies-plus-bursts rather than a pure turn-1-3 swarm — it plays more like a payoff-dense go-wide midrange-aggro than hyper-aggro. That's an intentional trade for interaction density at "competitive" power level. This build started with 9 cards clustered on turn 3 and was rebalanced during self-grill review (Fiend Hunter moved to sideboard, Cathar Commando moved to mainboard) to shift one slot down to turn 2.

decks.identity: Mono-White Voltron: suit up one resilient, evasive creature with recursive auras and efficient equipment, using Odric, Lunarch Marshal to spread granted keywords across the whole team.
decks.pitch: Deckbuilding math. Macro-Archetype: Aggro. Projected avg MV: 2.28. Lands: 15 (37.5% of N=40) -- above the 30-35% Aggro band on purpose: Voltron needs to both deploy a threat AND pay an Equip/activation cost in the same or following turn, so it wants slightly more mana consistency than a standard aggro shell. No cantrips, mana dorks, or land-MDFCs in the pool, so no downward modifier applied. Non-land split: Creatures 14 (56%), Auras/Equipment 8 (32%), Interaction 3 (12%) -- Threats/Payoffs and creatures are combined into one bucket in this archetype because the auras/equipment package *is* the win condition, not a side engine, which is why this deviates heavily above the standard 45-55% Aggro Threats/Payoffs band.

decks.identity: Mono-White aggro-tempo Voltron: cheap resilient/evasive bodies (several Human-typed) carrying equipment and auras, backed by exile-removal auras and protection instants
decks.pitch: Payload count and pip math. 5 Equipment pieces (Stitcher's Graft, Cobbled Wings x2, Butcher's Cleaver x2) live in a 24-card nonland shell — 20.8% of spells. Strength of Arms only makes its 1/1 Human Soldier token "if you control an Equipment," so by turn 3-4, once one of the five is down, it functions as a de facto two-for-one every time it's cast. That token is itself Human, so it benefits from Butcher's Cleaver's lifelink clause and — if Metallic Mimic named Human first — enters with a bonus +1/+1 counter.

decks.strategy: WB Lifegain-Counters/Voltron: convert repeatable lifegain triggers into permanent +1/+1 counters on Voice of the Blessed while black drain effects double-dip on the same death/lifegain events
decks.identity: White-Black Lifegain-Counters/Voltron midrange built around Voice of the Blessed as the single payoff for every lifegain source in the deck
decks.pitch: Slot allocation. Lands: 16 (40% of N=40) — squarely in the Midrange Land 38-42% band for this classification. Interaction: 4 dedicated removal spells (Tragic Slip, Infernal Grasp, Valorous Stance, Sever the Bloodline) plus Fiend Hunter and Slayer of the Wicked as removal-on-a-body and The Meathook Massacre as a sweeper — roughly 29% of the 24 nonland slots, appropriate for a competitive-power Midrange seat that needs to survive to its lifegain payoffs. Threats/Payoffs + Engine: the remaining ~17 nonland cards are almost entirely tagged Payload/Payoff or Engine/Outlet for the Lifegain and Counters (+1/+1) synergy clusters — this deck's engine budget is absorbed directly into its threat slots rather than run as separate value/ramp pieces, consistent with the Midrange proportions table.

decks.identity: Go-wide token/fodder generation feeding repeatable sac outlets into death-drain and card-advantage payoffs, capped by Liesa and Westvale Abbey as late-game finishers.
decks.pitch: Vampire density and Sorin. After swapping Gather the Townsfolk for Indulgent Aristocrat, the deck runs 5 Vampires (Blood Artist x2, Indulgent Aristocrat x2, plus Sorin, Imperious Bloodlord himself as a sac target for his own +1) - enough that his "if it's a Vampire, put a +1/+1 counter on it" and "sacrifice a Vampire" modes are live most games, rather than dead text.

decks.identity: White-Black go-wide tokens deck that converts cheap token generation and creature deaths (combat, sacrifice, or wraths) into life drain, card advantage, and counters-based finishers.
decks.pitch: Cheap token generators ([Gather the Townsfolk](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Gather the Townsfolk"), [Lingering Souls](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Lingering Souls"), [Thraben Inspector](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Thraben Inspector"), [Wedding Announcement](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Wedding Announcement"), [Ghoulish Procession](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Ghoulish Procession")) flood the board while [Blood Artist](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Blood Artist") / [The Meathook Massacre](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"The Meathook Massacre") / [Morbid Opportunist](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Morbid Opportunist") convert every creature death — yours or theirs, combat or otherwise — into life drain and cards. [Falkenrath Torturer](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Falkenrath Torturer") is the deck's one proactive sac outlet; everything else feeds off deaths that were already going to happen. [Cathars' Crusade](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Cathars' Crusade") and [Intangible Virtue](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Intangible Virtue") turn a wide-but-small board lethal in a turn or two, and [Skirsdag High Priest](https://scryfall.com/search?q=!"Skirsdag High Priest") converts two tapped bodies into a 5/5 flier once something has died.

decks.strategy: Mardu (W/B/R) meld midrange with a reanimator-lite subtheme
decks.identity: All three Innistrad meld pairs (Brisela, Hanweir the Writhing Township, Chittering Host) built as pure upside on top of a removal-and-recursion Mardu midrange shell; Through the Breach cheats Griselbrand in early, and its own sacrifice clause sets up a permanent Edgar's Awakening reanimation later.
decks.pitch: A grindy Mardu (W/B/R) midrange deck built to make all three Innistrad meld pairs functional at once. Bruna/Gisela (-> Brisela), Hanweir Garrison/Battlements (-> Hanweir, the Writhing Township), and Graf Rats/Midnight Scavengers (-> Chittering Host) are each independently playable, so completing any of them is pure upside layered on top of a real removal-and-recursion shell.

decks.identity: Mardu (W/R/B) reanimator-midrange built around cheating/reanimating Griselbrand, riding two independently-playable Innistrad meld pairs as value creatures
decks.pitch: The rare/mythic budget shapes the meld choice. With a hard cap of 5 rares/mythics across main+sideboard, all three Innistrad meld pairs couldn't fit: Hanweir Garrison + Hanweir Battlements alone cost 2 rare slots, and adding them to Griselbrand + Through the Breach + Bruna + Gisela would blow the budget. Graf Rats + Midnight Scavengers (melds into Chittering Host) is the "free" pair — uncommon/common, costs nothing — so it's an auto-include. The second pair had to be chosen: Bruna/Gisela (1 rare + 1 mythic) over Hanweir (2 rares), because Bruna's cast-trigger reanimation and Gisela's evasive body reinforce the reanimator plan, where Hanweir's token generation would have been an unrelated sub-theme.

decks.identity: Black-Red Vampire tribal go-wide aggro with a single-card White splash for Edgar Markov
decks.pitch: Slot allocation. Lands: 15 (37.5% of N=40) — above the 30-35% Aggro baseline, justified by the W splash for Edgar Markov and a genuine 6-drop top end, offset by seven Blood-token sources providing incidental filtering. Interaction: 4 removal spells (16% of 25 nonland) — slightly above the 10-15% Aggro guidance, defensible given this is a competitive-power cube seat where 2-for-1 removal spells (Bloodtithe Harvester, Voldaren Ambusher) are baked into creatures rather than counted as dedicated slots. Threats/Payoffs + Engine: the remaining 21 nonland cards are essentially all Payload/Payoff or Engine/Outlet-tagged Vampires — go-wide Aggro decks run almost entirely threats by design.

decks.identity: White-Green token swarm converted into lethal via anthem/counters payoffs (Cathars' Crusade, Second Harvest, Wedding Announcement, Intangible Virtue, Torens)
decks.pitch: Macro-Archetype: Midrange. Projected Avg MV: 2.58. Lands: 16 (40% of N=40) — Midrange band is 38–42%; no cantrip/dork/MDFC modifiers applied (0 cantrips, 0 dorks, 0 MDFC-lands in the 40). Interaction: 5 cards (Valorous Stance x2, Clear Shot, Angelic Purge, Cathar Commando) = 20.8% of 24 nonland — bottom of the 20–30% Midrange band, appropriate since the deck's own board presence (wide token count) doubles as its best interaction. Threats/Payoffs (absorbing Engine per the Midrange convention): 19/24 = 79.2%.

decks.identity: WG Token Midrange-Combo with Lingering Souls black splash. Cryptolith Rite converts tokens into mana for Second Harvest doubling and Cathars' Crusade exponential growth.
decks.pitch: Cryptolith Rite + Intangible Virtue is the deck's defining engine. Vigilance on tokens means they attack and still tap for mana post-combat. Every 1/1 token becomes a Birds of Paradise that also pressures life totals.

decks.identity: Green-White Human tribal go-wide aggro: cheap Human bodies and token generators (Gather the Townsfolk, Join the Dance, Torens) scaled up by the cube's two true Human anthems (Mayor of Avabruck, Hamlet Captain) and closed out by Crusader of Odric, Odric Lunarch Marshal, and Butcher's Cleaver.
decks.pitch: Why GW over the alternatives. Pipeline discovery found that "Humans matter" cards in this cube are mostly just Human-typed bodies with generic go-wide payoffs -- the only cards that say "Human" in a team-wide pump effect are Mayor of Avabruck and Hamlet Captain, both Green. That is the actual reason GW beats Mono-White (no true lord) and RW (better removal, but zero lord effects) for this specific archetype.

decks.identity: GW Humans go-wide tokens deck with a thin R splash for Hanweir Garrison; closes via Crusader of Odric scaling, Odric shared keywords, and Butcher's Cleaver lifelink.
decks.pitch: The go-wide -> payoff loop. Five independent token sources (Gather the Townsfolk x2, Wedding Announcement, Join the Dance, Torens' cast trigger, Hanweir Garrison's attack trigger) feed three payoffs that don't compete for the same resource: Crusader of Odric scales off raw creature count, Mentor of the Meek converts small bodies into cards, and Odric turns any single keyword on the board (first strike from Thalia, lifelink from an equipped Cleaver) into a team-wide keyword each combat. The deck doesn't need to draw its payoffs in any particular order - any token generator plus any payoff already does something.

decks.strategy: GW Humans go-wide tokens into +1/+1 counters, value midrange
decks.identity: Go-wide Human/token generation feeding Cathars' Crusade, Metallic Mimic, and Torens as counter-snowball payoffs, closed out by Crusader of Odric and backed by dual-purpose removal.
decks.pitch: The core loop. 13 of the 24 nonland cards are Human creatures (Hopeful Initiate, 2x Thraben Inspector, 2x Fiend Hunter, 2x Cathar Commando, 2x Crusader of Odric, 2x Mentor of the Meek, Torens, Tireless Tracker), plus Gather the Townsfolk, Join the Dance, and Torens itself all mint additional Human tokens. Metallic Mimic named "Human" turns every one of those ETBs into a free +1/+1 counter; Cathars' Crusade turns every one of them into a counter on *every* creature you control simultaneously. With 5 creatures already on board, casting one more creature or Gather the Townsfolk with Cathars' Crusade in play adds 6 total counters in a single trigger.

decks.identity: WU control deck using repeatable blink engines to convert ETB removal/tempo creatures into permanent answers while grinding card and board advantage.
decks.pitch: Macro-Archetype: Control. Projected Avg MV: 2.91.

decks.identity: White-Blue blink engines feeding Cathars' Crusade for a team-wide +1/+1 counter go-wide finish
decks.pitch: The core loop. Cathars' Crusade reads "whenever a creature you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control" — it doesn't care whether that creature is cast normally, blinked, or copied. That means Restoration Angel's flash blink, Conjurer's Closet's free end-step blink, Deadeye Navigator's repeatable {1}{U} blink, Essence Flux's 1-mana instant blink, Gather the Townsfolk's two tokens, and Cackling Counterpart's token copy are all independently "another counter for the whole team" triggers. Deadeye Navigator soulbonded to any cheap creature (even itself) turns a big blue mana turn into several counters at once — this is the deck's explosive top end, gated behind drawing the single copy of Cathars' Crusade.

decks.identity: WU Spirit-tribal tempo: flash flying Spirits (Mausoleum Wanderer, Spell Queller, Nebelgast Herald) disrupt while clocking in the air; a lifegain-into-counters sub-loop (Lunarch Veteran/Apothecary Geist -> Voice of the Blessed) and blink redundancy (Restoration Angel/Essence Flux) add resilience and a growing finisher.
decks.pitch: Macro-Archetype: Tempo. Projected Avg CMC: 2.08 (actual: 2.08).

decks.identity: White-Blue Spirit tribal tempo deck using repeatable blink engines (Restoration Angel, Conjurer's Closet, Deadeye Navigator) to re-trigger ETB value and stack permanent +1/+1 counters via Metallic Mimic.
decks.pitch: A dense Spirit tribal shell (12 Spirit-typed permanents) that leans on flash-speed evasion and repeated ETB triggers rather than raw stats. Four blink pieces — Restoration Angel, Conjurer's Closet, Deadeye Navigator, and cheap Essence Flux/Cackling Counterpart — turn every Fiend Hunter exile, Nebelgast Herald tap-down, and Metallic Mimic counter into a recurring resource instead of a one-shot. The gameplan is to out-tempo the board with taps and bounces early, then grind out a Spirit army that keeps growing permanently via Metallic Mimic counters and Battleground Geist's anthem, closing with Subjugator Angel's alpha-strike tap-all or a long Deadeye Navigator loop.
